However, students with a very good academic level are expected. Ranking(s) requested (if available). The non –degree exchange program is subject to a limited number of spots, therefore a selection of the best students is made for this program as well. Please note that a nomination does not necessarily imply the student’s admission. Language requirements For scientific courses in French and/or English, a B2 level is recommended. It should be necessarily certified by an official test for our Double Degree programme (See list of accepted tests and mimimum points required below). Exchange students do not necessarily need to provide language tests. Many 2nd year “cycle d’ingénieur” courses are taught in French. To be allowed to choose these courses, a minimal “Top” B1 “French as Foreign Language”* level is compulsory but a B2 level is recommended to feel at ease. For access to scientific courses in English, a minimum level of B2 in English** is required. Besides, for students following the Double Degree program, a B1 or B2 level in French (according to the language of the study tracks chosen) will be mandatory to get Telecom Paris Diploma. 2 * The proof of the French language proficiency includes the following external certifications: TCF: 400 pts; TEF: 400 pts; TFI: 600 pts; DELF B2 or B1(75/100) or a higher education degree obtained from a French-speaking institution (the degree has to prove that the language of instruction was French). **The proof of the English-language proficiency includes the following external certifications: First, Advanced or Proficiency Certificates from Cambridge, TOEFL ITP (institutional): 543 pts; TOEFL IBT (internet-based): 71 pts; TOEIC: 795 pts; IELTS: 5.5, Linguaskill: 160 pts; Cambridge English Certificate and APTIS: B2 level or a higher education degree obtained from an English-speaking institution (the degree has to prove that the language of instruction was English). All tests should not be more than 2 years old (or 5 years for DELF and Cambridge exams). Amount of credits completed per semester 30 ECTS / semester Double Degree programme 4 semesters (24 months), starting in September (Year 2 and Year 3 of the engineering curriculum,”Diplôme d’Ingénieur”). According to the agreement, some Double Degree students have the possibility to join the Year 1 of the Diplôme d’Ingénieur engineering curriculum. Other Requirements / Remark(s) - The Exchange Programme is only for students coming from a partner university of Telecom Paris and sharing an exchange programme or Erasmus agreement. - In case of an Exchange or Double Degree program, students have to be nominated by the partner university’s mobility programme coordinator. April 1, 2026 (nomination) and April 15, 2027 (application), for September 2026 intake for Exchange students (coming for the full AY 2026-2027 or for the Fall semester) or for European / North American Double Degree students - November 1, 2026 (nomination and application) for February 2027 intake for Exchange students coming for the AY 2026-2027 spring semester - September 15, 2026 (nomination) and September 30, 2026 (application), for September 2027 intake for Double Degree students (outside of Europe and North America). 4 Information required for nomination - Student name and e-mail address - Faculty or study field, as well as study program - Study level - Which term is concerned by the mobility Website for application information Required supporting documents https://www.telecom-paris.fr/en/international/international-students/application-resources Documents needed: - Statement of purpose - Resume - Transcript of grades and ranking if available - Copy of passport or Identity card - Identity picture - At least 2 recommendation letters - Language(s) certificates Application for Internships / Master thesis Internship requests are not managed by the International Relations office. Students interested in doing an internship in one of Telecom Paris’ laboratory have to contact the laboratory directly or an identified teacher or look for internship opportunities on the following page: https://www.telecom-paris.fr/en/the-school/job-opportunitie Accommodation Is on-campus accommodation available for incoming students? There is various students’ accommodation close to the school with different prices according to the type of housing. Cost per semester: approximately between 2500 and 4500€ (according to the type and place). For more information, students can visit our page about students’ housing: https://www.telecom-paris.fr/en/campus/campus-life/housing-and-dining Application procedure for accommodation Relevant contact and information will be sent to students who need accommodation. Arrival Information 5 Suggested Arrival date: Fall semester Spring semester 1 or 2 weeks before exchange program courses start. 4 or 6 weeks before courses start for students who take our French Summer Course. Coming a few weeks in advance also allows students to attend integration activities. 1 week minimum recommended before courses start (in case of Exchange Programme) Airport pick-up service available? No No Visa Information Are students required to obtain a student visa? Yes, if students do not have the European Union citizenship. What are the procedures? Relevant information on the websites below: https://france-visas.gouv.fr/en/web/france-visas/home https://www.campusfrance.org/fr/visas-et-cartes-de-sejour Health Insurance Non-European students will have to register on https://etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr/#/ upon arrival in France in order to be covered by the mandatory French medical insurance(CPAM) that covers a part of medical expenses while studying in France. European students will have to get a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) or a temporary certificate from relevant institutions of their home country, before their departure. Non-European students are required to subscribe to a private health insurance at least valid for the first two months, before their registration with the CPAM is effective. 6 In general, students can also subscribe to a complementary private insurance to get a more comprehensive reimbursement of healthcare costs. Financial For visa issuance, French authorities require financial guarantee of 615€ per requirement month (7380€ for a year). Health Insurance EU Students Citizens of EU members States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland are not required to enroll in the French National Healthcare IF they have a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). The EHIC must be valid until the end of their stay. EHIC will allow students to get their healthcare expenses reimbursed under the same conditions as if they were in their home country. EHIC should be obtain prior to arrival in France. European students who do not hold an EHIC must apply for the French National Healthcare like other international students. Non-EU Students Enrollment to the French National Healthcare known as « Sécurité Sociale » is free and mandatory. This will allow students to benefit from partial refund on healthcare expenses, on average 60%. All the registration process is done online once visa is obtained.
